title: Relative component-site equivalence over a geometric field
statement: Let X be affine, Ω algebraically closed, η:Spec Ω→X any map, and U→X an affine pro-etale object whose global-ring map is ind-etale across the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Put V=U×_X Spec Ω, S=π₀(U), Q=π₀(V), and r:Q→S. Use the canonical component geometric morphisms π_U,π_V of [def-zl-generic-component-data]. Then π_V inverse image is an equivalence. There is a natural isomorphism r⁻¹⋙π_V⁻¹≅π_U⁻¹⋙g⁻¹, where r⁻¹ is the actual slice overMapPullback and g is the first projection [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There is also a natural isomorphism q_Q⁻¹⋙π_V⁻¹≅p_Ω⁻¹⋙h⁻¹ for the second projection h:V→Spec Ω, where p_Ω inverse image is the fixed profinite point pullback [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. No genericity, irreducibility, or w-contractibility is assumed.

proof.text: Affine base change makes V affine and ind-etale over Ω. The classification of affine ind-etale Ω-algebras as locally constant functions and the spectrum homeomorphism identify V with Ω[Q], using its actual connected-component quotient.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the following coefficient paragraph

proof.text: Each affine ind-etale basis object over V is Ω[E], with its V-map corresponding uniquely to E→Q. Conversely every such profinite arrow induces an ind-etale algebra map. Finite jointly surjective families correspond to the affine fpqc covering families. Comparison on this cover-dense basis gives equivalence of sheaf categories. It is restriction along the canonical component functor: its locally ringed-space characterization identifies each E-test object with Ω[E]. Hence the inverse-image adjoint π_V⁻¹ is an equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the following coefficient paragraph

proof.text: For E→S, base change of U_E along V→U and V_(E×_S Q) have the same locally ringed space |V|×_S E and the same inverse-image structure sheaf from V. Uniqueness makes the identification natural in E. Restriction along these isomorphic test-object functors identifies the composite direct images. Take adjunction mates to get the required inverse-image square.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.13, diagram (4.4) and the following coefficient paragraph

proof.text: The same comparison for an absolute profinite E is V×_Ω Ω[E]=Ω[Q×E]. On the geometric-field profinite basis the structural map is therefore precisely E↦(Q×E→Q). Use the normalized geometric-field point adjunction and its profinite point factorization, then take mates. Empty V gives the empty profinite slice and the same formulas.
